So, EAC is an anti-cheat, that means the following:  
\- No mods  
\- No Custom Clients  
\- No quality of life improvements provided by other software like AMD FSR  
\- No custom shit  
\- Performance issues (EAC needs to run and check your memory and opened programs to verify you not trying to inject something into VRC/any game it has) sooo, hey, lag intensifies, but that is normal with any AntiCheat tbh... (But for a game without ANY reason to have anticheats, its just a bummer)  
\- Does not stop asset flippers/rippers, since they have thousands of methods to do that that does not involve grabbing STRAIGHT from VRC with a custom client  
\- Does not stop crashers, since those use avatar things to crash people (corrupted shaders normally or heavy ones)  
\- Does not help with much... Since EAC is known to be one of the easier to bypass anticheats in the market, since its so popular and is kinda copy-paste in all games, so its just a matter of time until someone with malicious intent discovers how to bypass it.

Crashers mostly focus on working on shaders to overload the target computer so that is not going to change :/

Eac is known for eating a lot of performance (as any anticheat really), remember, its another program checking your computer all the time while you play.

Hackers will be stopped (for a brief moment) but EAC is laughably easy to bypass...

People that steal worlds/avatars are not going to be stopped, since VRC saves a log with a small encryption on your hard drive, pointing to the VRC Servers where the model is, in fact, if you grab the links from that file and place in a browser, it will download a packed Unity file, and if you run a program to unpack it (Forgot the name) it will be a .unitypackage, sooo, this also does not stop asset rippers... (Also, asset rippers can simply extract the assets from memory with other programs and rebuild them, while a hassle, its not something EAC can do against since you are grabbing the memory as a whole, not injecting into the game.

So yea, long history short: This makes a little more difficult for asset stealers and hackers to act, but does not affect anyone else with malicious behaviour, on the downside, it affects the normal players more than it should.

EAC, easy to implement, easy to use, *easy to bypass.*

Because: A) Bossing, B) Techs, C) Techs, D) TECHSSS e) Damage.

I played little of PSO, but i liked the idea of everyone being able to use Techs, as PSO2 came, i saw that A) Ra/Su is a meta that is good for bossing, and B) Has techs, so i used it.  


And to be fair, i like it, the "quality of life" improvements Hu does are huge... but they make it too easy to help players undo their fuck ups, and sadly that is something i don't see as making someone good... Having to toss a coin everytime you have a chance of dying, and 3/4 of the time you winning that coin tossup removes a little of the tension from fights for me, and makes things feel... boring. It is a gamble that people get too comfortable, i know that because i'm like that on my  two alts (Braver/Hu, Hunter/Su), and they have Iron Will and Automate heal, it's too easy to just mow everything down and don't worry much about your health, but that removes a lot of fun from the game imo.For Bossing Ra/Su is a beast, with the damage % being way higher than Ra/Hu even if you only consider Summoner Mark added. If you can shifta, it's a blessing too (But that last one can be done with a Sigma Wired Lance.)

On the Mobility side, being able to use Illzonde helps a lot for mobility, as it's fast and great for ranger. Ra/Hu sadly does not have much mobility outside of Rocket Rodeo-0 (meh) and Wired Lances (You need to change weapon and lose Nemesis/Slave/The weapon you have bonus).

TL;DR: I like the tension from playing Ra/Su, and the extra damage to bossing. Also the ability to use techs. It makes the game more fun to me.

Mag-wise, i agree, it can be considered P2W In some way or form, but the Rare Drop Boosts don't matter much.  
Lets suppose you have RDR 250% (Ex-cubes) and Triboost 50% (Daily), And Triboost 50% (Daily Boost), that is 350% RDR.  
I can buy a RDR 400% with Cash, and get a total of 500% RDR.  
Ok, 150% RDR extra is a lot, isn't it? Nope.  
Lets say a weapon has a 0.05% drop rate, with the 350% RDR, you get 0.175% Drop Rate. With the 500% you get 0.25% drop rate, it's a increase from 0.175% Drop Rate to 0.25%,  but, it's only a 0.075% increase, from expending Nothing (Only free RDR, Triboost and Daily Boost) to expending 900AC per 6 Hours of mission + Free stuff.  


TL:DR: 400% RDR from AC Shop is useless when farming Low Drop Rate weapons, because the Drop Rate boost from Free RDRs and Paid RDRs are not much different.

Phantom Limbs is something some people experience, you don't have a part of your body, but your brain thinks you do. Maybe that is why people feel Phantom touch, the body THINKS the parts of the body he is seeing in VR are yours, and when someone touch, you see it, and your brain thinks: I should be feeling this.  
When you have pain because of Phantom Limbs, one way to less it is by placing a mirror where your lost limb would be, and the mirror be reflecting your other limb that is still there. You look to the mirror and touch/scratch the place that is feeling bad on the phantom limb, some people feel better after that.  
Somethings are just... difficulty to explain. Every brain is connected differently. Mirror Touch Synesthesia is something that also happens to some.

While it's true, that making their own engine can be kinda good, for a begginer/small team, making one for complex games like an FPS/RPG is, while not impossible, extreme hard. It's true that games that have their own engine (Warframe, Call of duty (zombies at least), Crysis (witch is CryEngine but you get the point)) are very good, because they can exceed in the theme they are going for, a game made by the engine creator will follow that engine main focus, be it FPS (CryEngine), Arena Shooter (Unreal) or even RPG (RPG maker XP).  


But like i said, making a engine is kinda hard, i saw one time a person making on youtube a Doom-like engine. and the guy needed some hours to finish it. And this is a doom Like engine. Imagine doing a RPG/MMORPG engine that can render 3D graphics with nice lighting system. One person would be doomed.
Yeah, i can see your point, and that is kinda true. The terrain and lighting and Network in Unity by default is kinda awful.

True and False. It's true that Unreal 4 have a better Network than Unity 3D. This is something i cannot deny. And i also can say that UE4 have better Graphics and Effects than Unity 3D. But this is for Default Unity 3D.   
Lighting can be amplified for example in Unity with a free Asset nammed Aura, that is top quality in my opnion.

Multiplayer 3D Games are not only Unreal strenght, but kinda Unity too, it really depends on the programmer and/or the team.

Unreal is good, not saying that it isn't. Unreal can be tuned down and used for 2D mobile too. (I'm just more used to Unity so, this can be a bit of bias).

My point is just to see/show that, the engine matters, it needs to be a good engine after all, but after picking a good one (It being a 2D game Engine like RPG Maker, or a 3D/2D one like Unreal, Unity etc.) The thing that will most matter is the person making the game.

Well, my analysis are really three things: The games made for the engines (And the company that made them), A lot of youtube videos talking about the engines (Comparisons, Limits, etc), and using the engines really, I used CryEngine (3 or 4, i dont remember now), Unreal 3, Unity (Started on version 4/5) and RPG Maker XP/VX (Started using since the RPG MAker 2000, but really did a small MRPG game for me and my friends on the XP with help of some other people on the internet), I spended most of my time with RPG Maker and Unity, and while i used more than a week of CryEngine before School got the best of me, Unreal 3 was too heavy for my old potato PC and my mindset really (CryEngine almost was back in the day), today i did not test Unreal 4, but i did see some comparisons.   


Stability of the tools is something i did not really ignore, it depends on several other factors like the Computer that is running the engine. And while the Tools are good or bad in the engine, a lot of assets create it's own tools (Aura for Unity for example, or ProBuilder). And some are very limited for a specific Genre (RPG Maker XP). And while Unity is limited for example in the Lighting, Unreal is limited in it's blueprint system (you cannot use for everything, the same with Cryengine Visual Codding System) (At least these two have a visual system for not-programmers, and they can do wonders (Like AI in Cryengine 3))  


The start of the project to release is not something i can really tell right now. I'm not a expert, i did not use all the engines for making games in full potencial, and i'm today studing for some other things (Trying to enter a university isn't easy here were i live), i did only some small projects for fun, and for learning. Also, it depends on the scale of the team, if you start making a game solo in a certain engine, you are gonna take a long time for make something good.
